issues.legal_issue: A co-owner may invoke the statutory pre-emption remedy against a stranger transferee of an undivided share in a family dwelling house during execution of a partition decree, until the decree is fully executed and satisfied.
material_facts: The property was found to be a dwelling house belonging to an undivided family.
A co-owner obtained a final partition decree for an undivided share and later gifted that share to a person who was not a member of the family.
The transferee sought execution of the decree, but the property had not yet been divided by metes and bounds or delivered into the respective shareholders’ possession.
A remaining family shareholder applied to buy the transferee’s share before execution was complete.
issues.conclusion: The application was maintainable: seeking execution of the partition decree to obtain separation and possession of the transferred share amounted to suing for partition. The right could be invoked while execution remained incomplete, but not after the decree had been fully satisfied by division and delivery of possession.
issues.legal_principle: Section 4 of the Partition Act, 1893, read with Section 44 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, protects members of an undivided family from a stranger’s entry into their common dwelling house by permitting a family shareholder to buy the stranger’s share. The words “sues for partition” are not limited to filing an original partition suit and include a transferee’s pursuit of execution of a partition decree. The court relied on CPC Section 38, Explanation VII to Section 11, Order 22 Rules 10 and 12, Order 21 Rule 16, and the explanation to TPA Section 52 in recognizing that litigation may extend through execution until full satisfaction. It approved Harendra Nath Mukharjee v. Shyam Sunder Kuer, Satya Narayan Chakravarty v. Biswanath Paul, and Boto Krishna Ghose v. Akhoy Kumar Ghose, and rejected the contrary view in Abdul Sathar v. Al Nawab. It applied a beneficial construction consistent with the provision’s purpose of preserving the peaceful enjoyment of a family dwelling house.

rule.if: partition_decree_execution and undivided_family_dwelling and share_transferred_to_outsider and outsider_seeks_partition and family_shareholder_undertakes_purchase and not decree_fully_satisfied

predicates.partition_decree_execution: The proceeding concerns enforcement of a decree ordering partition of property.
predicates.undivided_family_dwelling: The property is a dwelling house belonging to an undivided family.
predicates.share_transferred_to_outsider: A shareholder transferred an undivided share in the dwelling house to a person outside the family.
predicates.outsider_seeks_partition: The outsider seeks separation and possession of the transferred share, including by pursuing execution of a partition decree.
predicates.family_shareholder_undertakes_purchase: A shareholder who is a member of the family undertakes to buy the outsider’s share.
predicates.decree_fully_satisfied: The partition decree has been fully carried out by division of the property and delivery of the shareholders’ respective portions.

issues.definition: When a partition decree is being enforced concerning an undivided-family dwelling house, an outsider seeks separation of a transferred share, a family shareholder undertakes to buy it, and the decree has not been fully satisfied, the purchase application remains maintainable.

issues.legal_issue: The statutory pre-emption remedy for a stranger’s share in a family dwelling house ends once the partition decree has been fully executed and the respective shareholders have received possession of their separated portions.
material_facts: The court distinguished the pending execution in this case from a situation in which a partition decree has been fully executed.

It explained that after division by metes and bounds and delivery of possession, the common dwelling house ceases to belong to an undivided family for purposes of the stranger transferee’s separated portion.
issues.conclusion: After the partition decree has been fully executed and satisfied by division and delivery of possession, the statutory pre-emption remedy is no longer available against a later transfer of the stranger’s separated portion.
issues.legal_principle: Section 4 of the Partition Act, 1893, read with Section 44 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, applies while the property remains a common dwelling house belonging to an undivided family and the partition litigation remains unfinished. Once execution fully separates the portions and puts the shareholders in possession, the common dwelling-house character relevant to the remedy ends, the litigation reaches its terminus, and there is no remaining subject matter on which the remedy can operate.
